parole.testo: From Late Middle High German grūpe (Silesian, ca. 1400), from Old Sorbian and/or Old Polish krupa, from Proto-Slavic *krupa.

parole.significato: whim (capstan or vertical drum turned by draught animals)
parole.testo: From earlier Gepel, likely from Old Sorbian *gybadło (“movement tool”); compare Czech hýbadlo, Lower Sorbian gibadło and Upper Sorbian hibadłaŕ. First attested in the 16th century.

parole.significato: yes; yeah; expresses agreement or understanding
parole.testo: From a Slavic dialect, probably Sorbian. Compare Czech ano (“yes”), Polish no (“yeah; well”), Russian ну (nu, “yeah; well”). In the sense of a filled pause touching on etymology 1 above.
